workarounds.symptom: [Serve] gRPC servers keep SO_REUSEPORT on with enable_so_reuseport=False, so direct ingress ports can be shared
workarounds.workaround: Fix: [serve] Pass grpc.so_reuseport to gRPC as an integer. Target files: python/ray/serve/_private/grpc_util.py, python/ray/serve/tests/unit/test_grpc_util.py. `start_grpc_server(..., enable_so_reuseport=False)` did not turn SO_REUSEPORT off. It passed the option as the string `"0"`, and gRPC reads `grpc.so_reuseport` as an integer and ignores a string, which leaves its default (on). (Ref: https://github.com/ray-project/ray/pull/66816)

workarounds.symptom: [Train] prepare_data_loader drops a custom batch_sampler with more than one worker
workarounds.workaround: Fix: [Train] Raise in prepare_data_loader instead of dropping a custom batch_sampler. Target files: python/ray/train/v2/torch/train_loop_utils.py, python/ray/train/v2/tests/test_torch_trainer.py. `prepare_data_loader` rebuilds the DataLoader with a `DistributedSampler` when there is more than one worker. For a DataLoader created with a custom `batch_sampler`, the rebuild drops the `batch_sampler` and copies `batch_size=None`, so each worker silently gets one-sample items instead of batches. (Ref: https://github.com/ray-project/ray/pull/68201)

workarounds.symptom: [Data] `map_batches(zero_copy_batch=False)` does not copy NumPy batches when `batch_size` is omitted

Make `map_batches(zero_copy_batch=False)` copy batches when the caller uses the default `batch_size=None`. Previously the whole-block path passed through a read-only NumPy view, despite the caller explicitly opting out of zero-copy input. (Ref: https://github.com/ray-project/ray/pull/67154)

workarounds.symptom: [Train] LocalTrainUtilsFn.report() does not save checkpoint to RunConfig() storage_path
workarounds.workaround: Fix: [Train] Keep the last checkpoint after a metrics-only report in local mode. Target files: python/ray/train/v2/_internal/execution/train_fn_utils.py, python/ray/train/v2/tests/test_local_mode.py. In local mode (`ScalingConfig(num_workers=0)`), a `ray.train.report()` call without a checkpoint erases the last reported checkpoint. After it, `ray.train.get_checkpoint()` returns `None`, and so does `Result.checkpoint` when training ends on such a report. This PR keeps the last checkpoint, as distributed mode does. (Ref: https://github.com/ray-project/ray/pull/68070)
